To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the RTEM beta lactamase is inactivated by mechanism-based inactivating agents that form an acyl intermediate with the enzyme and that the acyl intermediate can react further to form a stable adduct with the enzyme.

the RTEM beta lactamase is inactivated by a variety of penam sulfone derivatives, and the reaction is consistent with a mechanism that involves nucleophilic attack of a serine residue (serine 70) on the penam sulfone.

the beta-lactams are potent inactivators and inhibitors of the RTEM and other beta-lactamases and that the inactivation of these enzymes by the beta-lactamas involves a covalent reaction with the serine hydroxyl of Ser-70.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of mechanism-based inhibitors of the beta-lacatmase of Escherichia colt.
the development of beta-lactam sulfones as mechanism-based inactivator of the beta-lacatamase.
the development of a new generation of mechanism-based beta-lactamases inactivators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
penam sulfones are mechanism-based inactivator of beta-lactamases.
the beta-lactams and penams, in their normal reactions, form a covalent acyl-enzyme with Ser-70.
a number of beta-lactam antibiotics and their analogs are mechanism-based inactivating agents of the beta-lacatamase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the penam sulfones are potent inactivators, and that they are likely to be mechanism-based inhibitors of the enzyme, in that they are poor substrates, but are potent inactivating agents.
